Position of the majority of young [sex of FGD] on the ladder of power and freedom (private rating): 5 = Power and freedom to make almost all major life decisions: 0 votes; 4 = Power and freedom to make many major life decisions: 10 votes; 3 = Power and freedom to make some major life decisions: 0 votes; 2 = Only a small amount of power and freedom: 0 votes; 1 = Almost no power or freedom to make decisions: 0 votes
Today we as youth work hard in order earn a living as different from the past whereby we used to depend on our parents alone.
The age we have reached allows to make decisions. Even the parents now trust us in the decisions we make.
Today the spread media has made us to learn a lot of things. We are able to learn from the radio, television as different from the past when the media was limited to very few people.
Through the films we watch, we normally see the way people suffer in making a living. This turns a challenge to us to work hard and make decisions.
It means one liberating himself or herself from ignorance.
[Another one?] Learning different issues concerning the human life and his surroundings.
Learning about the environment that surrounds us.
Learning the skills that can enable one to get employed as an agricultural extension officer for instance.
[Is it useful to get an education?] All respondents: Yes.
[Why?] Getting educated first of all enables one to be aware of the self and be able to make right decisions.
In school we get to learn how to maintain the environment that surrounds us.

[Another one?] Education enables us to earn some money at any time once opportunities emerge. For example it does not matter whether you have studied to the university, during the voting season for example for us who have completed form four, we were able supervise the voting exercise and we were paid for this work.
(All respondents come to an agreement that boys in this community do study to Form IV and that most of the girls do study to Form II.
[Why do girls end their studies at Form II?] Many girls end because of early pregnancies.
Girls end because of lack of school needs and other basic needs at home.

Some girls are compiled of family responsibilities in that she has to go to school and at the same time she has to take care of the family and at the end of the day they end up stopping studies. Also some girls have no parents and they are living with grandparents at the end of the day they do misuse the freedom they have with their grandparents and end up contracting pregnancies.
The distance to school also leads girls to stop early before they can complete form four.
[What level of education do you think boys of this village should have?] All respondents come to agreement that boys and girls in this community should at least study to the University.

[Why do you think boys and girls in this community should study to the university level?] After you have completed the university, you are sure that you can get employed because now you at least have a profession.
At the university level one can employ himself or herself in poultry keeping or teaching.
If girls study to the university level their chances to get early pregnancies are limited.
All respondents: Yes.

[Why do you think there is an equal consideration to both sexes in as far as getting educated is concerned?] Today parents no longer have biased beliefs whereby only boys were considered as potential saviors of their households. Today there are more examples where the girls who have been educated have saved their families from poverty.
For sure parents struggle hard to educate all boys and girls only that girls and some boys do discourage their parents by stopping in the way before completing the studies.
[What different agricultural activities do boys like to learn about when they are still young in this village?] They learn about different farming activities like the planting of maize and rice.
[Another one?] When we are young, we begin going with parents to the farm and do as they do until we are familiar with the farming activities.
When we are young we learn about growing vegetables for home consumption.
We do participate in the growing of cash crops such as pigeon peas together with the parents.

[What different agricultural activities do girls of your age learn about when they are still young in this village?] Girls in most of the time learn about how to prepare the farm and how to plant because after men have prepared the farm, they can only help to set up the holes for planting and the role for planting is normally left to girls.
They also learn about the harvesting and preparing the crops for storage.

[Which of these new agricultural practices have been the most important for the young men like you in the community?] (All respondents agree that the use of water pumping machines and farming by using tractors have been the most important farming practices during the past ten years).
[Why important?] The use of tractors makes the work easy meaning that if one use the tractor in farming, he or she can save time for other activities.
Farming by hand hoe also does not allow the water to get retained well in the soil. The farm that has been tilled using the tractor retains much water and leads to rich harvest.

[Why do you think that water pumping machines are important to young men like you?] Not only to young men but these are important to the whole community because now people are able to do tomato and water melon growing throughout the year.
All respondents: Yes.

All people are normally invited to participate into these new farming practices only that people do fail to respond out of their ignorance.

All respondents: Yes.
[How?] Men for example after farming, in the planting process the men only dig up the holes and women’s responsibility is to place the seeds and cover with soil.

[Why is it done this way?] It is distribution of labor but also I think it is because the setting of holes is a tiresome activity that needs men intervention since it would seem a tiresome activity to women.
Planting is taken as a simple activity to be done by women.

[What would happen if a young woman tried to grow and then sell maize on their own?] It is not easy for a girl still living with parents to grow maize and sell it on her own. She has to decide with the parents.

As long as she still lives with the parents, she cannot do that unless if for example she harvested eight bags of maize and she wants to sell some, she has to give reasons as to why she wants to sell but she has to sell some of them and leave some bags for home consumption but after the parents have consented.
If at all she lives alone and she is the decision make for that household, she can grow and sell maize on her own.
[What would happen if a young man tried to grow and then sell maize on their own?] Also he must be living alone or else he has started his own family in order to pass such decisions.
[Do we agree with him?] All respondents: Yes.
Very few families have this organization whereby each household member prepares his or her own plot.

[How is it decided who farms which plot?] These families normally allocate the each member his or her plot so as to ease the caring activities for these farms but other activities such as farm preparation, planting, weeding and harvesting is collectively done one plot after the other.
This is organized on a family basis meaning that each household has its own way of doing their activities. They will work to each plot until all plots are done.
[Does this organization vary by season or based on a certain type of crops?] All respondents: No.
This also differs from one household to the other but in most of the time women will work on their husbands though the household that grow crops separately are so limited.
They do work together.

During the farming season, although the labor is available, there is much competition for labor because many people are now doing farming and remember this community has people who come from other region to do farming so they demand labor for their farms.
[But you have said there have been an increased tractors usage?] These also have a high competition as they are on high demand but at the end of the day one can get to use them.
[So can we say that labor in this community is a big problem in this community?] All respondents: No.
[Why?] If you have money, there is no problem with getting labor. You can decide to get people or hire a tractor.

[What changes would you like to see in the village for the young men?] Employment opportunities must be increased. The government should establish agricultural processing industries that can absorb young men to work there.
The Non government Organizations that come to establish their activities here in the village should give the priority to young men first before they can employ outsiders.
If the young men get loans they can start business.
The government should find a good market for the agricultural products so that young men who do farming can benefit out of it.
[What changes would you like to see in the village for the young women in this community?] Young women too need to get employed just as young men do.
Young women should be taught entrepreneurship skill so that they can establish their own business.
Young women should be counseled to avoid getting deceived by men who never marry them but end up leaving them with children who later become a burden to them and parents.
